builder_plan.scenario: Your inference service slows down when several customers send requests together.
builder_plan.change: Replay a recorded request trace with only the proposed serving policy changed.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current scheduler on the same model and hardware.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Requests meeting your latency target, throughput, failures, and cost per successful request.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Thermal-Headroom Routing for Efficient Robot Perception in Extreme Heat
summary: This method replaces static thermal management policies (like fixed throttles or duty cycles) with a predictive routing policy that uses an RC thermal model to select optimal detector configurations and avoid processor throttling. It requires implementing a closed-form thermal forecasting model and maintaining a routing layer, which adds computational overhead and necessitates hardware-specific calibration of thermal parameters. The approach may fail if the thermal model does not accurately reflect real-world hardware behavior, as validation was conducted in simulation and on an Apple M5 without confirming actual hardware throttling.
rationale: This technique addresses thermal constraints in edge robotics, which is a specific hardware deployment problem, and while it offers clear benefits for extreme heat scenarios, it requires access to specific hardware configurations and thermal validation that may not align with standard cloud-based LLM inference or typical AI/ML engineering workflows.

claims.statement: This method replaces static thermal management policies (like fixed throttles or duty cycles) with a predictive routing policy that uses an RC thermal model to select optimal detector configurations and avoid processor throttling. It requires implementing a closed-form thermal forecasting model and maintaining a routing layer, which adds computational overhead and necessitates hardware-specific calibration of thermal parameters. The approach may fail if the thermal model does not accurately reflect real-world hardware behavior, as validation was conducted in simulation and on an Apple M5 without confirming actual hardware throttling.

Reduces deadline misses by 3.9-7.5 percentage points at ambient temperatures of 45-55°C compared to latency-aware routing; a separate experiment shows miss-rate reductions of 6.2-9.5 percentage points.
